chunks: From him, from Mu'alla, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Sulayman ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The successors (Awsiya') are the gates of God, Mighty and Majestic, through which one approaches Him; and had it not been for them, God, Mighty and Majestic, would not have been recognized; and through them, God, Blessed and Exalted, has established His proof upon His creation.

key_terms.أبواب الله: The gates of God — the Imams as the means by which one accesses divine knowledge and presence
key_terms.احتجّ: Established proof/argued — God's hujja (proof) against creation is constituted through the Imams
key_terms.الأوصياء: The successors/trustees — the Divinely-appointed Imams who received the Prophet's authority

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the Imams being the gates of God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates one of the foundational doctrines of Shia theology: the Imams as the 'gates of God' (abwab Allah). This statement declares that the Awsiya' (the Divinely-appointed successors — the Imams) are the indispensable intermediaries through whom God is recognized, and that God's proof (hujja) against His creation is established through them. The concept would have been deeply resonant for Imam al-Sadiq's companions in the 2nd century AH, who understood the Imams as the authoritative guides to religious knowledge during the Abbasid era when direct access to Imams was restricted.
word_analysis: and had it not been for them

en.hubeali: From him, from Moalla, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Suleyman Bin Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The successos<sup>asws</sup>, they<sup>asws</sup> are the doors of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic which He<sup>azwj</sup> can be accessed through these, and had it not been for them<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would not be recognised, and by them<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Argued upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 2. Mu‘alla has narrated from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Sulayman ibn Suma‘a from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Qasim from abu Basir who has said that Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said the following.

“The successors (of the holy Prophet (s.a.) are the gates to Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, through which people go to Him. Had they not existed, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, would not have been recognized. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, will present these successors as evidence against His creatures.”
